title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

sense.text: The topic is entitled Supper, War and Marriage. “Alleluia”: how many of you know what the word hallelujah means? Literally it’s praise to Yahawah. The yah at the end is abbreviated for the Most High’s name, and halal is praises. This chapter is still continuing on from chapters 17 and 18. John is continuing with the vision he is seeing, in chronological order, and he is going to jump back in the middle of the chapter.

“For he hath judged the great whore”: who is the great whore? Babylon, which is America. I want us all to get in the habit of speaking plain, because many Christian commentaries will tell you Babylon the great whore is Vatican City. Remember in Revelation 18 it said come out of her, my people, letting you know the people of God would be in Babylon. We’re not in Vatican City; how many Negroes are in Vatican City anyway? You might have three. “Which did corrupt the earth with her fornication”: her fornication is spiritual fornication, idolatry: her holidays like Christmas, her democracies, and the main idol, the image of the beast, Caesar Borgia, as students in the class answered. And all nations were confederate to destroy us and keep us in darkness and lies, so that we would not remember that we are Israel. “And hath avenged the blood of his servants at her hand”: all the servants of the Most High are accumulated here with the destruction of Babylon. That includes the servants from the time of Rome, our forefathers Peter, James, John and Paul, who were put to death. They didn’t pay for it yet; they are going to pay for it when Babylon is destroyed. Even the ones that put the Savior to death, like it says in Revelation 1, the Most High is going to make sure they all come back and get judged for that.

“And her smoke rose up for ever and ever.” How did the Lord judge the great whore, based on what we’ve read in the past two weeks? A brother in the class answers: the EU, the European Union, also called NATO, the ten common markets. Another speaker adds: a lot of people still got that Christian mentality. They hold the Bible in their hand, but they don’t understand that this Bible is literally talking about revolution on a serious level. During 9/11 you wouldn’t find one white Christian, one Edomite Christian, saying we forgive them in Jesus; they said hunt them down and kill everybody. It’s only the Negro and Latino who get on the news when their family is gunned down and say I forgive him in the name of Jesus. You say the Lord’s Prayer: thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth. If Christ’s kingdom is coming on earth, what do you think is going to happen to this kingdom here? He is going to destroy this mess. When Michael Brown was gunned down in the street, his father yelled out something like burn this place down, and they went after him for inciting a riot. That’s why they are trying to get rid of the Bible: as more Israelites pick it up, the true meaning is coming out.

precepts.why: “And the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.”

Read week before last. “And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore”: the ten horns are the ten common markets, the European Union, as the brother stated, and the whore is Babylon, the United States of America. “And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth”: verse 18 is really telling you it’s America. America is the one that rules over the kings of the earth, not the Vatican. The Vatican don’t go into the UN or any major meetings of nations and run their mouth; it’s America in all those meetings telling nations do this or don’t do that.

That’s a heavy, heavy verse. “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” A lot of our people want salvation, but a lot of them don’t want the destruction of their enemies. You will hear doctrines created to save the other nations; we cannot save them, brothers. You got to accept both. If you just accept the salvation part but don’t want the destruction of your enemy, you’re not reading the Bible; you’re in some kind of la la land. That is Christianity: love everybody. What about my grandma?

sense.text: “And the four and twenty elders and the four beasts fell down and worshipped God”: don’t ask me the names of the 24 elders; some things the Most High don’t reveal. The four beasts go to the four archangels.

“For the Lord God omnipotent reigneth”: let’s look that word up. Omnipotent: of a deity, having unlimited power, able to do anything; all powerful, almighty, supreme, most high, unconquerable, invincible.

Men love war. We don’t want to see love stories; we want war and destruction. Growing up we’d build up the toy blocks just to destroy them. When you see a little boy playing with a Barbie, that’s when you got a problem. “For the marriage of the Lamb is come”: out of this whole chapter, this verse is very potent; it will cover a whole lot. First let’s find out who the Lamb is marrying. “And his wife hath made herself ready”: we are the wife, men and women. The heaviest part of the whole verse is hath made herself ready. That is the problem with Israel: some of us think we ready, but we ain’t really ready. The one third of Israel is the wife, which includes men, women and children. It’s already prophesied; the numbers are already set. You can’t add to it, and you can’t take away from it.

precepts.why: “For I have espoused you to one husband”: Paul espoused the Israelites unto one husband. “That I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ”: he was presenting us as a chaste virgin to Christ.

“And, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads”: this is after the major destruction; Christ is with the 144,000 in the wilderness. That’s when he turns to us a pure language.

“Until the day that I rise up to the prey”: not you or me; the I is the Most High. “For my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation, even all my fierce anger.” “For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent”: in that day we are all going to know the name of the Lord. You’re not going to have this faction of Israelites pronouncing it Yahweh, this one Yahawah, this one Ahayah, this one Jehovah. In that day it’s going to be over: Christ is going to say this is the name, bam.

“Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God”: to be a pillar means you’re a leader. “And he shall go no more out”: meaning into captivity; that ain’t happening no more. “And I will write upon him the name of my God”: this goes with Revelation 14:1. “And I will write upon him my new name”: Christ says I’m going to have a new name in that day. So what you arguing about? Yahshua, Yeshua, Yahawashi; I hate you because you don’t say it the way I say it. Look how they argue over this; it’s no different than the Bloods and the Crips. You say Yahweh, he say Yahawah: Negro propaganda madness. Another speaker adds that it’s a childish mindset, and that Israel has been in all captivities and speaks different languages, so to bring Israel to one mindset he has to give us the pure language and the new name, where there is no mistake.

“And no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand”: only the 144,000 is going to be able to learn this Bible; this is the new song. “These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins”: it means two things. Number one, philosophies; and philosophies from the time of Adam came from Eve, the woman. Women generally go with the power under Babylon. Most women draw towards the white man; he’s the power in the earth, not you. They don’t look to you for any power, no authority, not even a paycheck. So it don’t mean they never had sex. Not defiled with philosophies, like Proverbs 5 and 7, where a wicked woman draws away the man. “For they are virgins”: they appear pure in the sight of the Lord. “These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth”: the 144,000 are not going to make excuses when the scriptures cut them; they’re going to say I’m going to get my life right, because I’m guilty of that. Some of you brothers can’t do this or that because your mama said this or your wife said that; the Lord can’t use you yet. “These were redeemed from among men”: the 144,000 is men, so stop it. The white man says 50/50; that’s why you ain’t going to be down. When the man gets his glory, the woman is going to get her glory. When the white man is in power, the white woman is happy.

What is the proof that it’s not talking about literal sex? “But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever”: Peter was the top apostle; the top three were Peter, James and John, in that order. Peter had a wife. Why didn’t Christ get upset and say, dag Peter, you messed up, why are you married? He didn’t say that.

Don’t you think Peter would be one of the 144,000? “Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel”: that’s proof that Peter and the other apostles are part of the 144,000; they’re the senior men, the leaders of the 144,000.
“Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away”: no matter what you have done, when you repent of your sins all your old sins are wiped away, gone.

Add this to your arsenal. “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”: why aren’t they condemned? Because no matter what they’ve done, the Most High said it’s done, it’s gone, I’ve forgiven him. You can’t even utter it before the Lord, but this brother or that sister did this; he don’t want to hear that.

“Turn, O backsliding children”: what made us backsliding was sin, Christianity, democracy. To backslide means you are going away from God and his laws; you are doing the moonwalk from his word. “For I am married unto you.” “And I will take you one of a city”: sometimes a whole city could be destitute of believers and there will be that one spirit. In the Book of Acts the Lord told Paul don’t go to this city, go to that city, because there you have many believers. “And two of a family”: the Lord ain’t looking for whole families. I get amazed when I see whole families come in; I’m waiting to see how long that’s going to last. Some of y’all come into this truth and find out your wife don’t believe, or the woman finds out her man don’t believe and is still going to strip clubs. Everybody ain’t coming in. I’m sorry about your grandmother; we always get emails about my grandmother, my auntie. “And I will bring you to Zion”: that small number.

“There be many created, but few shall be saved”: one third is a few; that’s not a lot. That’s why the Lord ain’t choosing everybody. You got to know your kids; I look at my kids, and from youth I know which have the spirit of faith and which don’t.
“Be ready to the reward of the kingdom, for the everlasting light shall shine upon you for evermore.”

“They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth”: what makes us ready, brothers? When we rejoice in God’s commandments. Remember Christ said blessed is he that is not offended in me. Some laws come out and people get offended; someone you don’t know from Adam thinks you are making a personal attack on them. “When need is”: and believe it or not, need is now, as we see our people getting shot in the streets. We’ve tried voting, democracy, Christianity, Islam, science and Egyptology, and it’s all garbage. Now the need is come for us to rejoice in God’s commandments; we as a people have never done that. We’ve rejoiced in white man’s religions, but never in the commandments; that’s why when you say Christmas is pagan, it’s new to them. “And when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word”: that’s how the bride maketh herself ready. We are the bride, Christ is the groom, and we are making ourselves ready by rejoicing in his commandments.

sense.text: “And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white”: you ever see people like the Nuwaubians, the Dr. York group? Anytime they want to appear righteous they wear white, and they be wicked as hell; they get it from this scripture. This is why women wear white on their marriage day: are you sure you should be wearing white? “For the fine linen is the righteousness of saints”: the bride made herself ready; she was obedient to God’s commandments. She, meaning the bride, which is the twelve tribes.

precepts.why: I want to talk about righteousness for a second; it goes with us making ourselves ready. “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”
Most of us that teach on the street go here to explain righteousness. “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments”: that’s what righteousness is.

A lot of y’all stumble through Romans 10. Brothers, when you start teaching you’ll get hit upside the head with this verse. “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth”: a brother in the class answers, the sacrificial law. When you sacrificed, your sins were to be forgiven; in Moses you got some sins forgiven but not all, and in Christ you got them all taken away. “That the man which doeth those things shall live by them”: if you could do those things under the old covenant you would live by them, but it was impossible for us to do it. “Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:)”: because you don’t believe the Son of God came, taught us and sacrificed his life for us.

sense.text: “Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb”: that’s a heavy verse. All of us are blessed, because all of us have been invited and called to the marriage supper of the Lamb, but the point is we have to make ourselves ready.
“For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy”: anytime you’re uttering the words of Christ, you’re speaking prophecy.

precepts.why: Christ gave us a parable on the same topic. “Which made a marriage for his son”: the king is the Most High, and the son is Christ. “And sent forth his servants”: the servants are the prophets, not other nations. “But they made light of it”: they made excuses not to go; one to his farm, another to his merchandise, his business. “And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.” “And he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city”: that’s the Roman armies; that’s 70 AD. God sent forth Rome against us; that’s his armies. “But they which were bidden were not worthy.” “Both bad and good”: bad Israelites and good Israelites came in. “He saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment”: remember the garment represents the righteousness, which is the keeping of the commandments. This dude was naked, meaning he was in the midst of sin. “And he was speechless”: he didn’t know what to say. “And cast him into outer darkness”: that’s destruction; kill him. “For many are called, but few are chosen.”
The servants are not other races. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants.”
The precept for the remnant that slew his servants. “O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets”: the Lord would have saved us a long time ago, but Israel was hardheaded.

“And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies”: Roman armies. “But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck”: the women breastfeeding babies were caught and murdered, and some were sold into slavery. “And shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Christ is telling you out of his own mouth that the people in the land are Gentiles, and the real Israelites went into captivity.

Christ didn’t say nothing new; he was quoting Moses and the prophets. Somebody might say Rome ain’t his armies; here’s the proof. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”: the symbol of ancient Rome was the eagle. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: their language was Latin. Write that down.
This goes with go ye therefore into the highways. “Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets.”

Why the wedding garment is heavy. Satan is talking to the woman, Eve. “And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food”: this tree represented idolatry, philosophies. “She took of the fruit thereof”: she learned it, she studied it. “And gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat”: she taught him. Eve learned something from the devil, went to her husband, usurped his authority, and said this is the real deal. That happens on a lot of levels today: the brothers will be trying to get themselves right, and then the woman brings her philosophy to him, and next thing you know he’s following the wife in evil instead of the Most High. “And the eyes of them both were opened”: their spiritual understanding. “And they knew that they were naked.” “And they sewed fig leaves together”: that’s for another class, where they tried to hide amongst the nations and be like the nations.
“For Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies”: Aaron made a golden calf and Israel started to pray to it. It’s a similitude; they were naked, meaning in the midst of sin.

“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them”: the coats of skin go into the righteousness, which represents the law. What law gave them forgiveness for the sins they committed? Sacrifice. It’s not talking about them literally being naked here.

sense.text: Verse 11 jumps back to what happened in chapters 17 and 18. “And in righteousness he doth judge and make war”: I love that, because a lot of times we don’t understand the characteristics of Christ. We think he’s some soft homeless guy who loves everyone and kisses everyone; none of that garbage is in the Bible. And the man that taught that, your friendly neighborhood white man, lives on war: praise the Lord and pass the ammunition. And you’re sitting up in Christianity passing him the bullets so he could kill you. The mindset has not changed since Exodus 15:3; Christ, I’m sending you back for war.

“His eyes were as a flame of fire”: this is how we know it’s Christ. “And on his head were many crowns”: that’s why he’s called King of kings. “And he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself”: so what you arguing about the name of the Lord for? Christ said I got a name that nobody knows but me.
“And his name is called The Word of God”: how come nobody argues about that? In the beginning was the Word; he’s the Word. In Hebrew, Ha Dabar.
“Clothed in fine linen, white and clean”: when they finish, them white garments ain’t going to be white; they going to be bloody red.

“And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations”: that’s the law; he was speaking the law, and the law is like fire, burning everything up: their planes, their jets, their missiles, rocket ships and satellites. Then there’s a part where he gets down on the ground and just starts killing people; that’s what makes his garments red. “And he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God”: that’s what we read in Isaiah 63:1-4.

precepts.why: “The Lord is a man of war”: now that’s heavy.

I started sending my kids to martial arts; y’all better learn how to fight. When y’all got beat up as kids, your parents said you ain’t coming in the house till you go out there and fight. “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”: “to teach them war”. The Most High is about war; I don’t know what Bible you’re reading. He said I want them to learn war: they have to know strategy, they have to know how to throw down.

Y’all read these Bible stories to your kids and get them all feminized; it ain’t no beautiful story, it’s history. “As the clay is in the potter’s hand”: we are the clay, and the potter is the Most High. “Good is set against evil, and life against death”: when the Most High makes man on earth, good must be set against evil. The Most High creates good and he creates evil; you better pray you on the good side. The white man says if you ever want to learn story writing, production and direction, read the Bible, because it’s our history, the foundation of everything. “And there are two and two, one against another”: no matter where you try to escape, you can’t escape that. You go to work and see evil; you go to your own family and see the same element. The Israelites are the good guys; Esau is the bad guy.

We always read this one, but I like the way it sounds. “A certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz”. “His body also was like the beryl”: beryl is green. “And his face as the appearance of lightning”: when you saw Christ, you saw power. “And his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass”: brass burned in a furnace. “And the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude”: Christ didn’t speak soft; when he spoke everybody heard him.

Another speaker in the class teaches this one: I get angry sometimes, but my anger is controlled; the scripture says be angry and sin not. “Who is this that cometh from Edom”: the Lord giving Isaiah a vision of himself coming to do damage, written as question and response. “With dyed garments from Bozrah”: Bozrah is the capital of Edom. “This that is glorious in his apparel”: people see a vision of Christ in a sheet; glorious means his garments were bad, decked out. “Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel”: in Revelation the blood rises up to the horse’s bridle; Christ is going to take his big black feet and smash people. I can imagine Nat Turner loved reading this. “For I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury”: this is controlled anger; he’s got select people he is smashing. “And their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments”: that’s why his garments are dyed red. “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart”: his mind is on one thing, war. That’s the day we’re looking for: let every wicked thing be put to death. If you ain’t trying to roll with this, I’d rather see you dead than see you trespass these commandments. “And the year of my redeemed is come.” Bishop: that was good.

About that sharp sword that goes out of his mouth. “And one shall undertake to fight against another”: when Christ returns the nations will be at war one with another. “And then shall my Son be declared”: so who said the Apocrypha don’t talk about the Son of God? “Every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another”: when they hear that trumpet they are going to say Houston, we have a problem; forget about fighting each other, we got to attack him. That’s Psalms 83; they are all confederate, because Christ ain’t coming to save any of them, he’s coming to save the Israelites. So these nations are not Christians, and they’re not your friends either. “And an innumerable multitude shall be gathered together”: all the armies of the world. “Being prepared and builded”: we read that in Revelation 19, the bride made herself ready. “And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: all of the white man’s science and technology. “Which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest”: that’s nuclear fire. “And he shall destroy them without labour by the law”: the law is like fire; that’s the sharp sword in Revelation 19:15.

sense.text: “And I saw an angel standing in the sun”: who said the angel had sex with Mary? An angel that could stand in the sun; she’d be burnt up. That’s really stupid, but you hear Muslims say that. “Come and gather yourselves together unto the supper of the great God”: this is the sacrifice; this is the supper.

“That ye may eat the flesh of kings”: the nations did that to us; when you read Psalms, they left our bodies on the ground and the birds came and ate us. So Christ said we’re going to do the same thing to them on a grand scale. That’s reap what you sow.

“And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth”: that beast is the white man. It ain’t just going to be the white man in his war; 2 Esdras 15 mentions the Arabs, Asia, Egypt, Assyria, a lot of nations. It’s just that the top nations are those Edomite nations, the ten horns that give their power unto the beast for one hour, from when the European Union was established in 1957, sharing their economics, the coal and steel community for weapons, and the atomic union for nuclear understanding.

“And with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him”: who is the false prophet? Students in the class answer: Caesar Borgia, the image they brought life to, and Esau who brought down the bombs. Both answers together. The false prophet that wrought miracles is the image of the beast that also dropped the atom bomb; it’s all together, not just the Vatican over here and democracies over there. “With which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast”: his philosophies. “And them that worshipped his image”: his Christianity, his religions. “Cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone”: this is where people get the hell notion from; they precept it with the parable of Lazarus and the rich man. The lake of fire is thermonuclear fire.
“And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.”

precepts.why: What we read two weeks ago, saying the same thing. “These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast. These shall make war with the Lamb.”

This is going to explain the false prophet that wrought miracles. “So that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men”: 1945, the dropping of the atom bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. “By the means of those miracles”: see what they’re calling it. “That they should make an image to the beast”: that’s Caesar Borgia, painted by Leonardo da Vinci as Jesus Christ. “Which had the wound by a sword, and did live”: Rome fell in 193 AD and did live in 1453; it was called the Renaissance. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: the life they gave that image was the life of Christ. “That the image of the beast should both speak”: in their movies, in their media; they find somebody that looks like Caesar Borgia and he speaks the words of the Bible. “And cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.”

The lake of fire is explained. “Reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men”: thermonuclear fire. “Not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance”: the Lord don’t want to kill all of us; he got one third, and he wants us to come to repentance. “But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”: when you least expect it. “The heavens shall pass away with a great noise”: boom. “And the elements shall melt with fervent heat”.

“Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes”: that’s the same thing 2 Peter was talking about, the same thing Revelation 19 is talking about: the lake of fire, thermonuclear fire.

Most people don’t understand what the day of the Lord is. “Howl ye”: that doesn’t sound like a day a lot of people want to be involved in. “It shall come as a destruction from the Almighty”: Jesus is coming to bring destruction. That’s why he said in Matthew 10:34, think not that I come to send peace on earth; I come to bring a sword.

Where are they going to be cast? “It shall not be quenched night nor day”: there are going to be parts over here in this country that will not be quenched night or day. “None shall pass through it for ever and ever”: you ain’t doing no business deals over here; you ain’t walking down the streets like that Will Smith movie, I Am Legend.

Verse 7 is a heavy scripture; I ain’t leaving it alone. This is a part of making ourselves ready. “What manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”: brothers and sisters, our conversation must be godly. That comes through trial and error, through application and rehearsal of the scriptures; that goes for men and for women. Some brothers want to come around us and talk stupidity; we don’t have time for foolishness. Some sisters do dumb and evil things; I’ve been in this truth 25 years, and anything you do, you bring stain on everything we’re trying to do.
